gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-nastaliq-urdu: Noto Nastaliq Urdu moves with a dignified calligraphic lilt, lines packed tight, drawn by a barely tilted nib. And Amadeus, stretched wide with joins that match its strokes, is the bolder voice against it.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-ahom: Amadeus stretches its words wide, every glyph drawn with a single-width stroke. Amadeus is the one for commanding display, while Noto Serif Ahom handles the reading, its brush stroke barely varying in pressure.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-armenia: Noto Serif Armenian has generous counters in every small letter, with a mild, approachable stroke contrast. And Amadeus does the shouting, one stroke thickness everywhere, built for display while the serif handles the text.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-balines: Stretched-out words and a plain, unmodulated outline make Amadeus feel bold and commanding. Noto Serif Balinese sits tall and traditional beside it, a middle-ground serif that softens that blunt outline.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-bengali: Wire-bent and wide, Amadeus forms each letter from one unbroken length of line, bold and commanding. Noto Serif Bengali settles into long text, hairlines tame and never razor thin.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-dives-a: Monoline, wide and bold: Amadeus stretches every word across the line. Noto Serif Dives Akuru then tucks in short-looking capitals and soft, modest curves, quieting things down after that blunt heading.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-gurmukh: Zero stroke modulation, with words stretched wide: that is Amadeus. Noto Serif Gurmukhi, literary and generous in x-height, changes weight gradually, so its lines feel steady yet faintly modulated.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-khmer: A blueprint's constant line, stretched wide and bold: that is Amadeus. Noto Serif Khmer brings tall lowercase close to its capitals and lighter horizontals, never threadlike, so the two sit comfortably together.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-todhri: Noto Serif Todhri reads sturdy, its thinnest curve points still carrying real weight. Down a full screen of text, its sizable x-height keeps lines legible, and Amadeus stays the wide-set voice above.
gen-dafont-arkhip-fs-nunito: Arkhip floats its letters well apart, every stroke uniform and geometric. Where Arkhip excels at crisp geometric display, Nunito, with generous round bowls, carries the more approachable, contemporary text.
